parsed.rationale: All three records — `SheetDraggingKey` in `WXUI/OverlaySheet.swift`, `ThemePickerActiveKey` in `Wallpaper/ThemePickerState.swift`, and `UITestingModeKey` in `Wallpaper/ThemePickerState.swift` — are structurally identical empty `type-alias-object` shells (shared_field_count: 1, differing_slots: null) solely because the SwiftUI environment/preference key pattern mandates a boilerplate-free type declaration for every distinct key. Their names encode entirely unrelated domain concepts (overlay sheet dragging, wallpaper theme picker activation, and UI testing mode), so the structural match is coincidental. Extracting them to a common package would couple `WXUI` and `Wallpaper` over semantically unrelated keys, and a macro would add a shared dependency to eliminate a one-liner declaration — neither trade-off is justified at this population size.
